answers.value: Only two of the four — Hedge Funds and Venture Capital — are Alternative Investment Funds
answers.reasoning: Under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 an AIF is a privately pooled investment vehicle that is not covered by the mutual fund or collective investment scheme regulations. Venture capital funds fall in Category I and hedge funds in Category III, so both are AIFs. Bonds and stocks are conventional (traditional) instruments traded on regular markets and are precisely what 'alternative' investments are defined against, so neither counts. The tally is two.

answers.value: Only buying/selling government bonds and buying/selling foreign currency are RBI income sources
answers.reasoning: The RBI earns from interest on and trading in government securities (open market operations) and from returns on and dealings in foreign currency assets, so I and II are income. Pension fund management is the PFRDA's domain, not the RBI's. The RBI lends to banks and to the government under the LAF/MSF and ways-and-means route, never to private companies. Printing and distributing currency notes is an EXPENDITURE item in the RBI's accounts (the cost of security printing), not a source of income, which rules out option D.

answers.value: Only two rows are correctly matched — the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and the Directorate General of Systems and Data Management
answers.reasoning: Row I is wrong in its third column: the Directorate of Enforcement does enforce the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (along with FEMA and PMLA), but it works under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, not the Internal Security Division-I of the Ministry of Home Affairs. Row II is correct — the DRI is the apex anti-smuggling agency enforcing the Customs Act, 1962, under CBIC in the Department of Revenue. Row III is correct — the Directorate General of Systems and Data Management sits under CBIC in the Department of Revenue and runs data analytics for tax administration. The judgement call is row III, whose analytics function overlaps with that of the DGARM.

answers.value: Only the second statement is correct — BRSR disclosures are largely non-financial
answers.reasoning: Statement I is wrong twice over: the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report is mandated by SEBI, not the Reserve Bank of India, and it applies to the top 1000 listed companies by market capitalisation, not to all listed companies. answers.value: Statement I is wrong (poultry and wool rearing income is taxable); Statement II is correct (rural agricultural land is not a capital asset)
answers.reasoning: Section 2(1A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 defines agricultural income narrowly around rent/revenue from land, cultivation and allied processing; poultry farming, dairy farming and wool rearing fall outside it and are taxed as business income, so the exemption under Section 10(1) does not reach them and Statement I is not correct. Statement II is correct: Section 2(14) expressly excludes rural agricultural land from the definition of 'capital asset', which is why its sale attracts no capital gains tax.

answers.value: Statements I and III are correct; India is not resource-rich in all 30 identified critical minerals
answers.reasoning: India joined the Minerals Security Partnership in June 2023, so I is correct. III is correct: the MMDR Amendment Act, 2023 inserted Part D in the First Schedule listing critical and strategic minerals and empowered the Central Government to auction mining leases and composite licences for them exclusively. II is plainly false — the very reason India identified 30 critical minerals in 2023 was its heavy import dependence for lithium, cobalt, nickel and rare earths.

answers.value: Both II and III are correct and both explain why bondholders face lower risk than stockholders
answers.reasoning: All three statements are true. Statement II explains Statement I because a lender holds a contractual claim to fixed interest and principal, whereas an owner holds only a residual claim on whatever is left over. Statement III explains it too, and more directly: in liquidation and in the order of servicing, debt is paid before equity, so the stockholder absorbs losses first. Option B is wrong because it inverts the direction of explanation, and D is wrong because both II and III are correct.

answers.value: Statements I and II are correct; the claim that no regulator warns investors or acts against unregistered advisors is false
answers.reasoning: India does account for an overwhelming share of global equity option contracts traded by number, and its market capitalisation did overtake Hong Kong's in early 2024 to become the fourth largest in the world, so I and II hold. Statement III is false: SEBI is precisely that regulator — it has published studies on individual traders' losses in the F&O segment, issued repeated investor cautions, and taken enforcement action against unregistered investment advisors and finfluencers.

answers.value: Both II and III are correct and both explain why a circular economy cuts greenhouse gas emissions
answers.reasoning: All three statements are true of a circular economy. Statement II explains Statement I because extracting, transporting and processing virgin raw materials is highly energy- and emission-intensive, so substituting recovered material directly lowers emissions. Statement III also explains it, since less waste per unit of output means less energy and material consumed and less waste sent to landfill, where decomposition releases methane. Option B, which allows only one of the two to be explanatory, is the runner-up and the reason this is a judgement call rather than a certainty.

answers.value: Statements I and II are correct; interest received on loans is a revenue receipt and creates no liability
answers.reasoning: Statement I is the standard definition of a capital receipt — it either creates a liability or reduces an asset of the government. Statement II follows from it: borrowing creates a liability and disinvestment reduces the government's asset holding, so both are capital receipts. Statement III is wrong on both counts — interest RECEIVED is income to the government, is classified as a revenue receipt, and creates no liability whatsoever; it is interest PAID that reflects an existing liability.

answers.value: Both statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy are correct
answers.reasoning: Roy was deeply learned in Sanskrit, Persian and Arabic, translated the Vedas and the Upanishads into Bengali and wrote extensively on Vedanta, so his respect for the traditional philosophical systems of the East is well attested — while he simultaneously held that modern culture was needed to regenerate Indian society. He equally championed rational and scientific enquiry, opposed superstition, and argued for human dignity and the social equality of men and women, most visibly through his campaign against sati and for women's rights to property and education.

answers.value: Three of the four — boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth, strict non-violence, and panchayats for settling disputes
answers.reasoning: The Non-Cooperation programme adopted at Calcutta and confirmed at Nagpur included boycott of British law-courts by lawyers and litigants and boycott of foreign cloth (I), and its constructive side included setting up panchayats to arbitrate disputes as a substitute for the boycotted courts (IV). Strict non-violence (II) was integral — Gandhi withdrew the entire movement after Chauri Chaura precisely because it was breached. Statement III inverts the programme: participants were to SURRENDER their titles and honorary offices, not retain them while refraining from public use. Hence three.

answers.value: A large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes
answers.reasoning: The name itself carries the answer: 'ara' means spoke and 'ghatta' means pot, so the araghatta is the spoked wheel fitted with pots that scoop water at the bottom of its rotation and empty it at the top — the ancestor of the Persian wheel. Option A describes the charas or mot, a leather bag drawn over a pulley by bullocks, which is a different device; options C and D describe simpler lift methods that involve no wheel at all.

answers.value: Mahendravarman I, the Pallava ruler
answers.reasoning: Mahendravarman I (c. 600–630 CE) is famous for the satirical Sanskrit farce Mattavilasa Prahasana, from which the title 'Mattavilasa' comes, and his inscriptions carry the epithets 'Vichitrachitta' (of curious mind) and 'Gunabhara', along with Chitrakarapuli and Chettakari. Simhavishnu was his grandfather, Narasimhavarman I his son and the conqueror of Vatapi (titled Mamalla), and Simhavarman belongs to the earlier Pallava line.

answers.value: Chandragupta II
answers.reasoning: Fa-hien travelled in India between roughly 399 and 414 CE, during the reign of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya, and his account Fo-kuo-ki describes a prosperous and lightly governed Madhyadesha. Samudragupta preceded him, while Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta ruled later — the Chinese pilgrim of Harsha's seventh-century court was Hiuen Tsang, not Fa-hien.

answers.value: Rajendra I of the Chola dynasty
answers.reasoning: Rajendra I launched the famous naval expedition of about 1025 CE across the Bay of Bengal against Srivijaya under its ruler Sangrama Vijayottungavarman, capturing Kadaram and other ports to secure the Chola trade route to China. The Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha, the Kakatiya Prataparudra and the Hoysala Vishnuvardhana were all inland powers of the Deccan with no comparable maritime campaign.

answers.value: Only two pairs are correctly matched — Asmaka–Godavari and Kosala–Sarayu
answers.reasoning: Asmaka (Assaka), the southernmost mahajanapada with its capital at Potana, lay on the Godavari, so I is right; and Kosala, with Ayodhya and Shravasti, lay on the Sarayu, so IV is right. Kamboja was a north-western janapada in the Hindukush region beyond the Indus, whereas the Vipas (Beas) flows through the Punjab plain, so II is mismatched. Avanti was centred on Ujjain on the Shipra and Mahishmati on the Narmada; the Mahanadi drains Chhattisgarh and Odisha, far to its east, so III is mismatched. Two correct.

answers.value: Lahore
answers.reasoning: Vishnu Digambar Paluskar founded the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya at Lahore on 5 May 1901, opening formal Hindustani classical music training to the general public and freeing it from the closed gharana-household system. He later established a branch in Bombay in 1908; Gwalior and Ujjain are associated with his training and travels but not with the founding of the school.

answers.value: District-level administration
answers.reasoning: Ashoka's Third Rock Edict directs the Pradeshika, the Rajuka and the Yukta to go on tour (anusamyana) every five years to propagate dhamma and inspect administration, and these three are conventionally placed at the level between the province and the village. The Pradeshika headed a district, the Rajuka handled rural administration, land assessment and later judicial powers over the countryside, and the Yuktas were subordinate revenue and accounts officials attached to them. Provincial charge lay with the kumaras or viceroys, and the village had its gramika, which is why A, C and D are excluded.

answers.value: Both statements about the Non-Cooperation Movement are correct
answers.reasoning: At the Nagpur session of December 1920 the Congress amended its creed so that its objective became the attainment of Swaraj by all legitimate and peaceful means, which is Statement I. Statement II records the movement's staged design accurately: it opened with surrender of titles and boycott of courts, schools, councils and foreign cloth, and the harder measures of mass civil disobedience and non-payment of taxes were reserved for a later stage, to be taken up only if Swaraj had not been won within a year and the government had answered with repression.

answers.value: Only four are NATO members — Bulgaria, Croatia, Sweden and North Macedonia
answers.reasoning: Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004, Croatia in 2009, North Macedonia in 2020 and Sweden in March 2024, giving four. Austria is not a member — it is constitutionally neutral under its 1955 declaration and is only a Partnership for Peace participant. Serbia is likewise outside NATO, having declared military neutrality in 2007, and its relationship is limited to Partnership for Peace cooperation.

answers.value: The Andes pass through four of them — Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela
answers.reasoning: The Andes run the length of South America's western margin through seven countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. Of the six listed, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela are on that list — Venezuela through the Cordillera de Merida, the range's northern extension. Brazil lies east of the range and is dominated by the Amazon basin and the Brazilian Highlands, and landlocked Paraguay consists of the Gran Chaco and the Parana lowlands, so neither is crossed.

answers.value: The equator passes through none of the three water bodies
answers.reasoning: Lake Tanganyika lies wholly in the southern hemisphere, its northern tip reaching only about 3 degrees south, so the equator misses it — the East African lake the equator does cross is Lake Victoria. Tonle Sap is in Cambodia at roughly 13 degrees north, well inside the tropics but far from the equator, and the Patos Lagoon lies on the coast of Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil at about 30 to 31 degrees south. None of the three is intersected.

answers.value: All three statements about Indian turmeric in 2022-23 are correct
answers.reasoning: India is the world's largest producer, consumer and exporter of turmeric, accounting for the bulk of global output and trade, so I holds. More than thirty varieties of turmeric are cultivated across some twenty states, so II holds. Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are the leading producing states, as recorded in the material issued around the constitution of the National Turmeric Board, so III holds. The item turns on recalled production figures rather than on reasoning, which is why this is not marked HIGH.

answers.value: All three are cited as evidence of continental drift
answers.reasoning: All three are standard evidences advanced for Wegener's continental drift. The belt of ancient rocks of about 2,000 million years along the Brazilian coast matches a corresponding belt in western Africa, showing the two coasts were once joined. The placer gold deposits of the Ghana coast have no source rock in situ and are held to have been derived from the Brazilian plateau when the landmasses lay side by side. And the Gondwana sequence of sediments, with its tillite base recording ancient glaciation, is found with counterparts across six landmasses of the southern hemisphere.

answers.value: Dust is indeed more concentrated over subtropical and temperate areas, but the reason is that these areas have MORE dry winds, not less
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct: dust concentration is highest over subtropical and temperate regions and lower over equatorial and polar regions. Statement II inverts the cause. Dust is lifted and held aloft by dry, turbulent winds, so it is precisely because subtropical and temperate belts experience abundant dry winds (and little washout by rain) that they carry more dust; equatorial regions have heavy convectional rainfall that scavenges dust from the air, and polar regions have little loose surface material. Saying these areas have 'less dry winds' contradicts the very mechanism that produces Statement I.

answers.value: Both are correct, and the warmer January ocean air is exactly why isotherms bend poleward over oceans and equatorward over land
answers.reasoning: January is Northern Hemisphere winter. Land has a low specific heat and cools quickly, while the ocean retains summer heat, so at any given latitude the sea is warmer than the continent. A line of equal temperature must therefore run further south (equatorward) to find that temperature over land, and further north (poleward) to find it over the sea, which is exactly Statement I. Statement II states this land-sea thermal contrast, so it is not merely true alongside Statement I but is its cause, making A correct rather than B.

answers.value: Statement II alone is correct and explains Statement I; Statement III is false because clay is in fact highly porous, just not permeable
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct: chalk is a permeable rock and clay is effectively impermeable. Statement II is correct and is the explanation for the chalk half of Statement I, since chalk's open pore network lets it take in and transmit water. Statement III is the trap and is false: clay has very high porosity, often 40 to 60 per cent void space, but its pores are microscopic and poorly connected, so water cannot pass through. Porosity and permeability are different properties, and clay is the standard illustration of a rock that is porous yet impermeable. With III false and II true and explanatory, only option C fits.

answers.value: All three greenhouse-effect statements are correct
answers.reasoning: Statement II is correct: it is the heat absorbed and re-radiated by the atmosphere that holds Earth's average surface temperature near 15 degrees Celsius. Statement III is correct: carbon dioxide, water vapour and methane absorb outgoing longwave radiation strongly, which is what makes them greenhouse gases. Statement I states the standard consequence, that without this blanketing the surface would fall far below freezing, the usual figure quoted being about minus 18 degrees Celsius. The word 'everywhere' is loose, since an airless Earth would also lose the atmosphere's heat redistribution and its sunlit face could be hot, but the claim is the one made in the standard textbook treatment and is intended as correct here.

answers.value: Both statements about the Rashtriya Gokul Mission are correct
answers.reasoning: Statement II states the Mission's founding purpose accurately: launched in December 2014, the Rashtriya Gokul Mission is aimed at development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds through scientific and holistic breeding and rearing. Statement I states the official rationale for its pro-poor character, namely that most low-yielding indigenous animals are held by small and marginal farmers and landless labourers, so raising their productivity directly raises rural incomes. Both are correct, so C.

answers.value: Both II and III are correct, but only III, the calcination of limestone to lime, explains cement's large share of global CO2
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct, since cement accounts for roughly 7 to 8 per cent of global CO2, comfortably more than 5 per cent. Statement II is correct as a description of the raw mix, as silica-bearing clay or shale is blended with limestone. Statement III is correct and is the actual reason for the emissions: in the kiln, calcium carbonate decomposes to calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, and this calcination releases CO2 from the rock itself, contributing more than half of cement's footprint before any fuel is burnt. Merely mixing clay with limestone releases no CO2, so II does not explain I and the answer is B, not A.

answers.value: Only Statement III is correct, and the concern about health-system resilience is why India did not sign; the Declaration is not binding
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct: India did not join the COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health. Statement II is false, because COP declarations of this kind are political and voluntary, carrying no legal obligation to decarbonise any sector. Statement III reflects the reason India actually gave, that commitments to cut emissions from health facilities could constrain the cooling, refrigeration and power-intensive infrastructure on which the resilience of its health-care system depends. So exactly one of the two supporting statements is correct and it does explain Statement I, which is option C.

answers.value: Both II and III are true statements, but only the equatorward migration of meltwater explains the shift in Earth's rotation and axis
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct, as studies of polar motion show the rotation axis drifting and the length of day changing. Statement III is correct and is the mechanism: melting polar ice moves mass from high latitudes towards the equator, altering Earth's moment of inertia and shifting the pole. Statement II is also a true statement in itself, since flares and coronal mass ejections do deposit enormous energy in the thermosphere, but that energy acts on a thin outer gas layer and does not redistribute the planet's mass or move its spin axis. Two correct statements with only one explanatory gives B.

answers.value: Both II and III correctly describe Article 6 and both are why it is so heavily discussed
answers.reasoning: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement has two limbs and both statements name one of them. Article 6.2 and 6.4 establish cooperative approaches and a centralised crediting mechanism, that is the architecture of international carbon markets, so Statement II is correct. Article 6.8 establishes a framework for non-market approaches between countries, phrased in the Agreement itself as being in the context of sustainable development and poverty eradication, so Statement III is correct. Both limbs are precisely what makes Article 6 the most negotiated and most discussed provision in climate and sustainable-development forums, so both explain Statement I.

answers.value: The Asian Development Bank launched the Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific
answers.reasoning: The Nature Solutions Finance Hub for Asia and the Pacific was launched by the Asian Development Bank, announced at COP28, to mobilise finance for nature-based solutions across its developing member countries. The name itself carries ADB's signature regional formulation 'Asia and the Pacific', which is how ADB frames its mandate; AIIB is infrastructure-focused, the New Development Bank is the BRICS bank with no Asia-Pacific regional remit, and the IBRD is the World Bank's global arm.

answers.value: All three uses of Direct Air Capture are correct: sequestration, industrial and food uses, and synthetic aviation fuel
answers.reasoning: Direct Air Capture extracts CO2 from ambient air, and what happens next defines its uses. Statement I is correct because the captured CO2 can be injected into geological formations for permanent storage, which is carbon sequestration and is the main climate rationale for the technology. Statement II is correct because captured CO2 is a feedstock for polymers and plastics and is used in food and beverage processing, for example carbonation and chilling. Statement III is correct because CO2 combined with low-carbon hydrogen yields synthetic hydrocarbon e-fuels, the leading route to low-carbon aviation fuel that does not depend on biomass.

answers.value: Only II and III are correct; the Peacock tarantula is an arachnid, not an omnivorous crustacean
answers.reasoning: Statement I is false on two counts: the Gooty or Peacock tarantula, Poecilotheria metallica, is a spider and therefore an arachnid, not a crustacean, and it is a predator feeding on insects and other small animals rather than an omnivore. Statement II is correct, as the species is endemic to a very small patch of reserve forest in Andhra Pradesh and is listed Critically Endangered precisely because of that tiny range. Statement III is correct, since Poecilotheria are arboreal, sheltering in holes and crevices of tall trees rather than in ground burrows.

answers.value: Only II and III are correct; India's per-capita CO2 is around 2 tonnes, far above the 0.5 tonne claimed
answers.reasoning: Statement I is false by a wide margin: India emits roughly 2.5 to 2.9 gigatonnes of energy-related CO2 for a population of about 1.4 billion, giving close to 2 tonnes per capita, about four times the 0.5 tonne figure in the statement. Statement II is correct, as India is second only to China for CO2 from fuel combustion in the Asia-Pacific region. Statement III is correct, since electricity and heat generation, dominated by coal, is by a large margin India's biggest emitting sector, ahead of industry and transport.

answers.value: Three pairs are correctly matched: cassava, ginger and Malabar spinach; mint and papaya are wrong
answers.reasoning: Cassava, Manihot esculenta, is a perennial woody shrub one to three metres tall, so I is correct. Ginger is a herbaceous perennial whose aerial shoot is a pseudostem formed of rolled leaf sheaths, so II is correct. Malabar spinach, Basella alba, is a succulent herbaceous twining climber, so III is correct. Mint is a perennial herb, not an annual shrub, so IV is wrong on both the life-span and the habit. Papaya is an unbranched, soft-stemmed short-lived plant usually classed as a giant herb or herbaceous tree, not a woody shrub, so V is wrong. That leaves three correct pairs.

answers.value: Only statement II is correct: marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria supply about half the world's oxygen
answers.reasoning: Statement II is correct and is the accepted figure, with marine phytoplankton and photosynthetic bacteria such as Prochlorococcus producing at least half of atmospheric oxygen. Statement I is therefore false, since it reverses the comparison: the ocean out-produces the rainforests, and mature rainforests in any case consume through respiration and decay nearly as much oxygen as they generate. Statement III is false and inverted: air is about 21 per cent oxygen, equivalent to roughly 300 milligrams per litre, whereas even well-oxygenated surface water carries only about 8 to 10 milligrams per litre, so water holds many times less oxygen than air, not more.

answers.value: All three are alternative powertrain vehicles
answers.reasoning: An alternative powertrain is any drivetrain that replaces the conventional internal combustion engine running on petrol or diesel. A full battery electric vehicle drives on stored electricity, a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle generates its electricity on board from hydrogen, and a fuel cell-electric hybrid combines a fuel cell with a battery. None uses a conventional combustion powertrain, so all three qualify.

answers.value: None of the statements is correct, because each says 'all types' of UAV and fixed-wing UAVs break every one
answers.reasoning: Each statement is a universal claim about all UAVs, so a single class of exception falsifies it, and fixed-wing UAVs are that exception throughout. Statement I fails because conventional fixed-wing drones land on a runway or are recovered by net, parachute or arrester, not vertically. Statement II fails because a fixed-wing aircraft must maintain forward airspeed to generate lift and cannot hover at all, automatically or otherwise. Statement III fails because many UAVs, especially larger military and long-endurance types, run on internal combustion or turbine engines, and others use solar or hybrid power, so battery is not the only source.

answers.value: Three of them, cobalt, lithium and nickel, are cathode materials; graphite is the anode
answers.reasoning: In a lithium-ion cell the cathode is a lithium metal oxide, most commonly nickel-manganese-cobalt or nickel-cobalt-aluminium chemistry, so lithium, cobalt and nickel are all cathode constituents. Graphite is the standard anode material, into whose layers lithium ions intercalate during charging, and it is not part of the cathode. That gives three of the four listed elements.

answers.value: All three contain plastic
answers.reasoning: Cigarette butts contain plastic because the filter is made of cellulose acetate, a synthetic polymer, which is why butts are among the most abundant plastic items collected in litter surveys. Most modern eyeglass lenses are plastic polymers such as CR-39 or polycarbonate, which have largely displaced glass. Car tyres are built from synthetic rubber, itself a petroleum-derived polymer, and tyre wear is one of the largest sources of microplastic released into the environment. So all three qualify.

answers.value: All three can be produced using coal gasification, though the nitroglycerine link runs indirectly through ammonia and nitric acid
answers.reasoning: Coal gasification yields syngas, a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen that is a versatile chemical feedstock. Ethanol is produced from syngas by catalytic or fermentation routes, and coal-to-ethanol is an announced Indian project, so I holds. Urea is the clearest case, since syngas hydrogen makes ammonia and ammonia plus CO2 makes urea, so III holds. Nitroglycerine is the doubtful one: it is nitrated glycerol, and the connection to coal is only through the nitric acid, which is made from coal-derived ammonia, a route also used for coal-based ammonium nitrate explosives in mining. Because that link is indirect rather than a direct product of gasification, the intended answer could equally be 'only two', and this item should be treated as unsettled.

answers.value: CL-20, HMX and LLM-105 are all military high explosives
answers.reasoning: All three are nitrogen-rich energetic organic compounds developed as high explosives. HMX, or octogen, is a long-established military high explosive; CL-20 is a more powerful caged nitramine developed as its successor; and LLM-105 is an insensitive high explosive designed to resist accidental detonation. Options C and D are the near-misses, because HMX and CL-20 do also appear as ingredients in solid rocket propellant formulations, but LLM-105 is purely an insensitive explosive and is not a propellant fuel, so the characteristic common to all three is that they are explosives, not fuels. Option A is unrelated, as none is a refrigerant.

answers.value: I and III are correct; Majorana 1 is Microsoft's chip, not AWS's
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct, as the Majorana 1 chip is a quantum processor built on a topological architecture and is intended to make scalable quantum computing possible. Statement II is false, because Majorana 1 was announced by Microsoft in February 2025; Amazon Web Services announced a separate quantum chip called Ocelot. Statement III is correct, since deep learning, which uses multi-layered neural networks, is a subset of machine learning, which is itself a subset of artificial intelligence.

answers.value: All three statements about monoclonal antibodies are correct
answers.reasoning: Statement I is correct: monoclonal antibodies are antibodies, which are proteins, produced in the laboratory from a single clone of cells rather than arising naturally in the patient. Statement II is correct in the sense intended, since a monoclonal antibody binds one specific antigen and thereby marks the target for the immune system, recruiting effector mechanisms such as antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity and complement activation. Statement III is correct: the monoclonal antibody m102.4 has been used against Nipah virus, including doses procured by India during Kerala outbreaks, and monoclonals were widely used against COVID-19.

answers.value: None of the three statements is correct; each is a false universal negative
answers.reasoning: Statement I is false, as marine viruses are the most abundant biological entities in the ocean, present at around ten million particles per millilitre of seawater. Statement II is false, since bacteriophages are viruses whose entire life cycle depends on infecting bacteria. Statement III is false, because altering host gene expression is central to how viruses replicate, with many viral proteins directly hijacking or shutting down host transcription. All three are sweeping 'no virus can' claims and each is contradicted by basic virology, so none is correct.

answers.value: Both II and III are correct, and together they explain why activated carbon is both a good and an attractive remediation tool
answers.reasoning: Statement I makes two claims, that activated carbon is 'good' and that it is 'attractive', and each supporting statement answers one of them. Statement II is correct and explains why it is good: an enormous internal surface area, often above a thousand square metres per gram, gives it a high adsorption capacity for heavy metals and organic pollutants. Statement III is correct and explains why it is attractive: it can be prepared cheaply from carbon-rich wastes such as coconut shell, rice husk and other agricultural residues, which keeps costs low and turns a waste stream into a product. Since both supporting statements bear on Statement I, the answer is A rather than B.

answers.value: Statements I and III only: an Ordinance can amend a Central Act and can be given retrospective effect, but it cannot abridge a Fundamental Right
answers.reasoning: Article 123(2) gives an Ordinance the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, so it can amend or repeal any Central Act (I correct) and, like an Act, can be made to operate from a back date (III correct). But Article 123(3) declares an Ordinance void so far as it makes any provision Parliament could not itself enact, and Article 13(2) bars Parliament from making any law that abridges a Fundamental Right; hence II is wrong. Options A, B and D all include II and therefore fail.

answers.value: Only two pairs are correct — Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura; the Nagaland pair is wrong because Nagaland was created by an ordinary Act of Parliament, not a Constitutional Amendment Act
answers.reasoning: I is correct: Itanagar takes its name from the Ita Fort ('ita' = brick), and Arunachal Pradesh has exactly two national parks, Namdapha and Mouling. III is correct: Tripura was a Part 'C' State, became a Union Territory under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (with the 7th Amendment abolishing Part C States) and became a full State in 1972. II is wrong: Nagaland came into existence under the State of Nagaland Act, 1962 — an ordinary law under Article 3, which Article 4 expressly says is not a constitutional amendment; the 13th Amendment only inserted Article 371A conferring special provisions. The State that actually came into existence through a Constitutional Amendment Act is Sikkim (36th Amendment, 1975). This is the contentious statement of the item — some prep material loosely credits the 13th Amendment with 'creating' Nagaland — hence MED.

answers.value: Only one — the Inter-State Council; the National Security Council and the Zonal Councils are not constitutional bodies
answers.reasoning: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 by a Presidential order issued under Article 263, so it is constitutional. The National Security Council was created in 1998 by an executive resolution of the government — neither constitutional nor statutory.
